q1_issues.issue: The fused compound `sky_cat` carries no genus atom, but Compound concepts makes `(Inheritance sky_cat cat)` mandatory ("the genus itself is always emitted either way"), exactly as the parse does emit it for `nightmoth_population`.

The subject of "reduces" is the hunting eventuality, not the kind `sky_cat`, so `(Reduce sky_cat nightmoth_population)` states a different claim and drops the mediating hunting; the relational-generic licence for a kind-level head also requires a bare kind-denoting NP on each side, which a gerund clause is not.

Asserts as a standalone generic habit — one skolem hunt event for every sky-cat at strength 0.9 — what the sentence only presupposes in its gerund subject, and the rule is left unconnected to the reduction claim.

q2_gaps: a gerund / nominalized clause in SUBJECT position ("Sky-cats hunting reduces nightmoth populations"): the instruction set has no pattern for an event-denoting nominalized subject, and its one nearby route, the relational generic / kind-level relation, is triggered only by bare kind NPs on both sides
notes: The parse falls into two disconnected halves — an unstated generic hunting rule and a kind-level Reduce atom — so nothing in it records that it is the hunting which reduces the populations. Decomposition of `nightmoth_population` (genus emitted, noun modifier not exposed) is correct.
